title: Quantile fuse bench jot
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal log for the "quantile fuse" run — trying to see whether merging high- and low-priority request traces into a single arrival stream (fused quantile sampling) smooths p99 without hurting median too much. Tossing down raw notes before I forget the oddities.

Hypothesis:
- If we weight sampling by recent tail occurrences and interleave short low-priority bursts, we can reduce tail amplification when the system hits transient micro-saturation.
- Secondary: a small amount of prefix KV-cache priming for fused traces should preserve median but may slightly increase median due to more cache churn. Need numbers.

Environment:
- Cluster: dev-fleet-3 (heterogeneous: 2x A100-80GB + 4x A10G), model pinned: gpt-medium-open-2024:rev-3
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.18.2 (local build w/ quant_kernels enabled)
- Load generator: benchflux v0.9.7 (local) with custom arrival adapter (quantile-fuse mode)
- Routing: single-region, no fallback, no model variants, direct to GPU
- KV cache: enabled default window=512, cache-size=12GB per worker

Workload profile (what I injected):
- 70% small (tokens: 16–64), 25% medium (128–256), 5% large (512–1024)
- Priority lanes: high (50% of requests), low (50%) but in bursts
- QPS sweep: 100, 200, 400, 700, 1000 (target qps measured at API ingress)
- Arrival patterns: poisson baseline, fused-quantile (my new adapter), and control mixed (round-robin mix of high/low)

Key metrics captured:
- p50, p90, p95, p99 latencies (ms)
- tail amplification factor = p99 / p50
- kv-cache hit-rate (per-worker)
- GPU util% (avg), tokens/s
- error rate (timeouts / 5xx)

Run notes (raw chronological):
1) 2025-01-18 10:20 — baseline poisson run at 400 qps. p50=28ms, p90=62ms, p95=95ms, p99=230ms. tail amplification=~8.2. Cache hit=78%. No errors.
2) 2025-01-18 10:45 — control mixed (RR) at 400 qps. p50=32ms, p90=68ms, p95=110ms, p99=290ms. tail amp=~9.1. Cache hit fell to 71%.
   - Observation: simple interleaving increased p99 and reduced hit-rate. So naive merge hurts tail.
3) 2025-01-18 11:10 — quantile-fuse adapter at 400 qps. p50=34ms, p90=66ms, p95=102ms, p99=170ms. tail amp=~5.0. Cache hit=75%.
   - Observation: p99 improved a lot vs control and baseline, p50 slightly worse. Healing effect visible.
4) 2025-01-18 13:00 — sweep to 700 qps, poisson baseline. p99 jumped to 460ms, errors started at 800 qps. Cache hit 61%.
5) 2025-01-18 13:30 — fused-quantile at 700 qps. p50=60ms, p90=140ms, p95=210ms, p99=330ms. tail amp ~5.5. Errors: transient timeouts <0.05%.
   - Note: fused mode kept tail lower than baseline but median increased more at high qps.
6) 2025-01-18 14:10 — enabled conservative cache-priming for fused traces (+prefetch on first 2 tokens on low-priority bursts). At 700 qps: p50=72ms, p90=150ms, p95=230ms, p99=300ms. Cache hit=69%.
   - Tradeoff: median up ~12ms vs fused without priming but p99 improved slightly.

Summary table (selected rows, rounded):
- 400 qps:
  - poisson: p50 28, p95 95, p99 230, hit 78
  - rr: p50 32, p95 110, p99 290, hit 71
  - fused: p50 34, p95 102, p99 170, hit 75
- 700 qps:
  - poisson: p50 55, p95 260, p99 460, hit 61
  - fused: p50 60, p95 210, p99 330, hit 64
  - fused+priming: p50 72, p95 230, p99 300, hit 69

Interpretation / quick conclusions:
- The quantile-fuse arrival adapter reduces p99 significantly compared to naive mixing. It seems to avoid creating contiguous micro-saturation pockets that amplify tail.
- Median (p50) tends to increase under fused arrival, particularly at higher qps and when priming is enabled. So there is a median vs tail tradeoff.
- Cache priming reduces p99 further at cost of higher median and a small recovery in hit-rate (weird but reproducible: priming reduces cache thrashing by making low-priority bursts more cache-friendly?). Need to study access patterns.
- At very high qps (>=800) we still run into errors — fused logic delays the onset but doesn't remove it. Need autoscaling or admission control for that regime.

Open questions / next runs:
- Can we make the fuse policy adaptive: pick fusion intensity based on recent tail amplification (local feedback) rather than fixed quantile thresholds?
- More granular cache telemetry: per-token-key reuse curve. Current hit-rate is too coarse.
- Try same experiments with quantized kernels off vs on (possible interaction with context-switch overheads).
- Try mixing with dedicated reserved capacity vs pooled heterogeneous to see if fused benefits are fleet-dependent.

Artifacts to save/attach:
- benchflux raw traces: s3://redwood-dev/perf/quantile-fuse/2025-01-18/*.json
- flamegraphs: s3://redwood-dev/perf/quantile-fuse/graphs/
- GH PR with adapter: github.com/redwood-inference/benchflux/compare/quantile-fuse

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add per-request KV access histogram to benchflux output (low priority)
- [ ] Write small doc for Ops: how to enable quantile-fuse in canary (and rollback knob)
- [ ] Run controlled test on dedicated pool (schedule with SRE)

Notes to self: keep design of fuse adapter minimal: do not preempt high-priority lanes for long. Try micro-threshold of 25ms windows. Also check scheduler wakeup times — observed small periodic spikes that might coincide with GC in benchflux (need to instrument client).

Unfinished thoughts (brain dump):
- Could combine with small admission controller that probabilistically drops large low-priority requests when tail amp > threshold. Might be nicer than raising median across the board.
- There may be a relationship between 'burstiness spectrum' and model KV cache decay; short-lived bursts amplify misses nonlinearly. Possibly we can keep a tiny LRU for recent low-priority tokens to reduce eviction thrash.

Endnotes:
Saving this as a personal jot. Will upload cleaned summary to Confluence after the dedicated-pool run.

-- Aditi
